**SSI Labs | UNSW | Founding Cohort, T3 2026**

**9 positions available |** **Unpaid extracurricular** **| In-person at UNSW**

SSI Labs (Student Systematic Investment Labs) is recruiting students for our founding cohort.

We're a student-led quantitative finance research group at UNSW, bringing together students interested in financial markets, statistics and software development to build, backtest and evaluate systematic trading strategies using real market data.

Members work in small project teams, developing research ideas, testing strategies, building technical infrastructure and reviewing each other's work.

The initiative is supervised by a UNSW finance lecturer with 15 years of industry experience as a Head of Trading.

Available Streams

**1. Markets & Quantitative Research (3 positions)**

* Research financial markets and identify systematic trading opportunities.
* Develop hypotheses and turn research ideas into testable strategies.
* Analyse backtesting results, market behaviour and risk.
* Present findings and participate in peer reviews.

**2. Statistics & Validation (2 positions)**

* Evaluate the statistical reliability of trading strategies.
* Conduct out-of-sample testing and robustness analysis.
* Investigate overfitting, market regimes and risk-adjusted performance.
* Work with researchers to improve models and testing methodology.

**3. Software & Data Analytics (4 positions)**

* Develop Python-based backtesting and research tools.
* Build and maintain financial market data pipelines.
* Develop analytics, visualisations and research infrastructure.
* Collaborate on debugging, testing and improving software reliability.

Who We're Looking For

Applications are open to **current University students from any degree or year**.

Backgrounds in finance, actuarial studies, mathematics, statistics, computer science, engineering, information systems and data science are particularly relevant, but not required.

Prior experience in quantitative trading is not necessary. We value analytical thinking, technical curiosity, initiative and the ability to work collaboratively.

Commitment & Eligibility

* **9 positions available across three streams**
* **Exclusively for current University Students**
* Weekly in-person research meetings at UNSW
* Approximately 8 to 10 hours per week, including collaborative project work
* **Unpaid extracurricular opportunity. This is not employment or a paid internship.**
* **Research and simulated paper trading only.** SSI Labs is a non-profit student initiative and does not manage investment capital.

As part of the founding cohort, you'll have the opportunity to contribute to real research projects while helping establish the research practices and infrastructure that future SSI Labs cohorts will build upon.

Pay: $1.00 per year

You will join a research community of more than 70 people focused on MND, with access to state-of-the-art facilities, advanced imaging and preclinical models, and an active Early Career Researcher network ('EnCouRage'). * Undertaking and assisting with a range of cellular biology and preclinical research projects, including work in cell and zebrafish models
* Participating in, and assisting with, data management and analysis
* Updating and maintaining databases for project samples and research data
* Contributing to day-to-day laboratory management, including equipment, consumables and record keeping
* Building effective working relationships with a diverse range of researchers, professional staff and students

An exciting opportunity exists to join the Drug and Alcohol Service for the Illawarra Shoalhaven Local Health District.

  

**Where you'll be working**

Wollongong Hospital is the Illawarra and Shoalhaven’s major referral and teaching hospital and has a bed base of more than 500. The campus, which incorporates the Illawarra Regional Cancer Care Centre, provides a comprehensive range of inpatient, outpatient and community-based services.

  

Wollongong is located an hour’s drive south of Sydney on a narrow coastal strip bordered by the Royal National Park to the north, Lake Illawarra to the south, the Tasman Sea to the east and the Illawarra Escarpment to the west. Learn more about the lifestyle benefits of living and working in Wollongong.

  

The Shoalhaven area is one of the fastest growing areas of NSW with over 5,000 new residents making the move here every year. The area has plenty to offer with the beautiful beaches of Jervis Bay, rainforests of Kangaroo Valley and tourist townships like Berry, all within 30 minutes’ drive.

  

Shoalhaven Hospital is a busy rural hospital which employs over 1,000 staff and is the main acute care hospital for the Shoalhaven region, providing emergency care, medical, surgical and orthopaedic services. Shoalhaven Hospital has an Intensive Care Unit focusing on high dependency and coronary patients, Children’s Ward and Maternity Unit as well as a purpose-built regional Cancer Care Centre and sub-acute Mental Health Unit. Shoalhaven Hospital is currently undergoing a $438 million redevelopment.

  
  

**What you'll be doing**

The ISLHD Drug and Alcohol Service provides broad-based training and experience in Addiction Medicine and is a training site for the Chapter of Addiction Medicine (FAChAM). The Addiction Medicine Unaccredited Trainee will, under supervision, provide medical assessment and access to treatment programs for Drug and Alcohol dependent people residing in the Illawarra (regional) and Shoalhaven (regional and rural) communities. This position will target marginalised drug users who may have co-morbid medical or psychiatric conditions and a wide range of training opportunities will be available including:

* Core addiction specialty learning
* Pain management
* Substance use in pregnancy
* Consultation and Liaison
* Education and research
  

The successful applicant will gain exposure and experience in the following areas under appropriate supervision:

* General Medical and Mental Health Drug and Alcohol Consultation Liaison.
* Outpatient Clinic: in which the principle focus is on individuals receiving Hepatitis Treatment program.
* Drug and Alcohol outpatient settings including assessment and ambulatory withdrawal management service including alcohol pharmacotherapy treatment.
* Tailoring the patient’s withdrawal management treatment to one of the following options available; hospital, community residential or outpatient or supported home withdrawal management.
* Prescribing maintenance pharmacotherapies for opiate dependent clients.
* Involvement in research opportunities.
  

This position is suited to General Practice Trainees (with a special interest in addiction), BPT trainees who may wish to complete their FAChAM training, or an experienced Trainee seeking a new opportunity within the Department. The clinical care will be delivered with consultation and inclusion of the multidisciplinary team within the Illawarra Shoalhaven Local Health District D&A Service. The position is community based and provides service delivery across the District.

Allocated Days Off (ADO) – once a month take a paid day off (eligible full-time employees)

Salary packaging – less tax and more take-home pay

* Novated leasing – lease a car and pay for all running costs out of your pre-taxed salary (eligible full-time employees)
* Fitness Passport - discounted gym membership that both you and your family can enjoy (eligible employees)
* Employee Assistance Program (EAP) – free confidential and professional assistance for staff and their families
* Discounted health insurance is available through a number of different private health insurance providers. Talk to your provider today for more information
* Career progression and professional development

You'll manage a varied musculoskeletal and sports caseload, and you'll be supported the whole way as you develop your clinical reasoning, hands-on treatment and exercise prescription skills. * Musculoskeletal and sports physiotherapy
* Manual and hands-on therapy
* Exercise-based rehabilitation
* Strength and conditioning
* Clinical assessment and reasoning
* Injury prevention and return to sport
* Patient communication and education

You'll also work alongside our network of GPs, orthopaedic surgeons, specialists and radiology providers, which is a good way to get exposure to the wider healthcare system early in your career.

* A recent physiotherapy graduate, or graduating soon
